rv.q: Certainly the last major London revival – a brooding, rap-battling affair directed by Jamie Lloyd – was a case in point. James McAvoy starred as Cyrano, the brilliant wordsmith with an obtrusively big schnozz.
A beautiful, romantic production that says more than the words alone ever could.
Fiercely funny and intensely romantic, Cyrano lives by his words and his sword.
The team have doubled down on the heartbreak of politesse in the face of a cautiously held but unrequited love, creating perhaps one of the most moving endings to a production of Cyrano ever staged.
What Simon Evans and Debris Stevenson have created here is nothing short of spectacular, with Adrian Lester’s leading turn delivering a performance for the ages.

cn.t: The RSC's Cyrano de Bergerac wins raves for Adrian Lester's superlative performance and high-energy staging. Critics praise the modernized wordplay and vibrant production, calling it a scintillating revival that exceeds expectations.
